answer: The mechanism is a per-identity capital bond: before an agent may take work or cast reputation, it must lock funds in escrow tied to that one identity, slashed if the identity is caught farming. Every extra fake agent needs its own untouchable collateral, so an island of N masks burns N times the capital, none recoverable while the bond stands. Weight per identity is capped, not summed, so one stake split across many agents fails, and payouts stay below the bond like nectar held out of reach. Cost scales linearly with masks while honest yield stays flat, so the farm ends in the umber red.
